<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9076fec29b4dc03f">Why search cross-stage recipes instead of one learning rate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aagentic-rec-tune">AgenticRecTune: Multi-Agent with Self-Evolving Skillhub for Recommendation System Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / Discover</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retrieval, fusion, and reranking shape each other&#x27;s distributions. Agents propose and review quality/diversity/risk across the recipe, with evidence for each stage and end-to-end effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Diversifying ranker scores cannot help if retrieval never provides varied categories.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:agentic-rec-tune" data-paper-title="AgenticRecTune: Multi-Agent with Self-Evolving Skillhub for Recommendation System Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf6384e67bb84496">Why require Critic, SkillHub, and real feedback after an Actor proposes a winner?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aagentic-rec-tune">AgenticRecTune: Multi-Agent with Self-Evolving Skillhub for Recommendation System Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / Discover</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Proposals are hypotheses. Critic checks feasibility, runs supply evidence, and Insight/Skill record conditions and failures. Self-ratings are not results. Local search is bounded and selection must isolate test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Record a diverse but over-budget configuration so future rounds avoid repeating it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.26969">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.26969-agentic-rec-tune/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf6384e67bb84496">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:agentic-rec-tune" data-paper-title="AgenticRecTune: Multi-Agent with Self-Evolving Skillhub for Recommendation System Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-288104c3ee63595c">How does SkillHub differ from restarting each round with the same prompt?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aagentic-rec-tune">AgenticRecTune: Multi-Agent with Self-Evolving Skillhub for Recommendation System Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / Discover</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It retains auditable feedback-backed constraints and strategies, reducing repeated failures. One high score is not automatically reliable and transfer depends on context.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Carry forward the finding that one diversity setting hurts new users.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.26969">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.26969-agentic-rec-tune/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-288104c3ee63595c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:agentic-rec-tune" data-paper-title="AgenticRecTune: Multi-Agent with Self-Evolving Skillhub for Recommendation System Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-66fce010d5e556b6">How prevent test tuning across three local rounds?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aagentic-rec-tune">AgenticRecTune: Multi-Agent with Self-Evolving Skillhub for Recommendation System Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / Discover</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Actor proposes bounded genomes and Critic selects only on validation, then saves evidence. Run test once after final selection. No real online authority is involved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not switch winners after seeing a disappointing final test score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.26969">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.26969-agentic-rec-tune/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-66fce010d5e556b6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:autolr" data-paper-title="AutoLR: Automating the Path from Research to Launch Review in Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-autolr-f0e06ba6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-44f52b6cb732a632">Why does AutoLR&#x27;s long-term state machine distinguish offline evaluation, real A/B testing, and Launch Review?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aautolr">AutoLR: Automating the Path from Research to Launch Review in Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Offline results apply only under their data protocol; real user effects and deployment resource constraints need separate verification. The state machine separates proposals, experiments, reviews, and promotion, records failures and budgets, and increases the evidence at each stage. LLM reasoning or code generation cannot grant approval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An optimizer with better validation but excess memory stops offline. A candidate with real experiment evidence can enter launch review, not automatically become the live champion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04871">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.04871-autolr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-44f52b6cb732a632">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:autolr" data-paper-title="AutoLR: Automating the Path from Research to Launch Review in Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-366e4daee96ef43b">Why does AutoLR not let the LLM directly save its preferred idea as the long-term champion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aautolr">AutoLR: Automating the Path from Research to Launch Review in Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Noisy proposals and deliberations can compound when language judgments alone make KEEP decisions. The LLM does semantic reasoning; a deterministic controller handles budgets, metric extraction, guardrails, and state transitions. Only evidence passing the relevant experimental gates can update the champion, and a proxy win does not bypass later A/B testing or Launch Review.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If an LLM suggests an optimizer whose offline benefit is unstable, log the proposal and failure and retain the old champion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04871">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.04871-autolr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-366e4daee96ef43b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:autolr" data-paper-title="AutoLR: Automating the Path from Research to Launch Review in Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-abf2dd6ec5a95be2">What trade-off does AutoLR&#x27;s disagreement penalty make compared with choosing only for exploration value?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aautolr">AutoLR: Automating the Path from Research to Launch Review in Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pure exploration favors unknown, risky ideas. Scoring existing evidence, exploration uncertainty, and expert disagreement gives conflict an explicit cost. Disagreement does not establish error; it calls for more evidence or lower budget priority. The local run did not beat the baseline in three rounds and could retain the champion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Of two equally novel ideas, test the broadly accepted one first under a tight budget and gather evidence about the contested one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04871">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.04871-autolr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-abf2dd6ec5a95be2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:autolr" data-paper-title="AutoLR: Automating the Path from Research to Launch Review in Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-47ac2230b7116bba">How does local AutoLR resume a disk ledger without using historical test scores for promotion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aautolr">AutoLR: Automating the Path from Research to Launch Review in Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Proposals can see research evidence and the completed validation ledger. Run one real backward-pass check, train under a fixed budget, and evaluate test only once after selection. Restore candidate, review, and validation state, keep `online_authorized` false, and do not feed test results back as selection rewards.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After an interruption, resume round three from prior validation records. If the final test regresses, report it instead of feeding the score into the proposal prompt and selecting again.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04871">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.04871-autolr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-47ac2230b7116bba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:coral" data-paper-title="CORAL: An LLM-Native Harness for Production Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-coral-3b3ed34a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c6fbfac3347e3e68">Why does CORAL require structured objectives and budgets rather than free-form LLM optimization advice?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acoral">CORAL: An LLM-Native Harness for Production Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A system must verify, execute, and compare configurations. Budgets define legal allocations and objectives translate observations into feedback. A successful loop is not by itself production causal evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Asking for more retrieval compute is not executable until channels and amounts are specified and checked against the cap.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.02730">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.02730-coral/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c6fbfac3347e3e68">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:coral" data-paper-title="CORAL: An LLM-Native Harness for Production Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-89bd6b73ca40a757">Why does CORAL project configurations onto a budget-feasible set and retain only recent experiment memory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acoral">CORAL: An LLM-Native Harness for Production Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>LLM proposals can contain negative allocations or exceed quotas. Projection creates executable candidates before real feedback informs the next round. Short memory helps adapt to change and limits stale guidance but does not justify deleting audit records. Feasible proposals still need quality validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If three retrieval allocations exceed a request cap, adjust them before testing. After traffic shifts, an old optimum should not automatically dominate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.02730">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.02730-coral/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-89bd6b73ca40a757">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:coral" data-paper-title="CORAL: An LLM-Native Harness for Production Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b9b80dc33e148828">When is CORAL&#x27;s short memory preferable to retaining the all-time best configuration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acoral">CORAL: An LLM-Native Harness for Production Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Recent feedback is more useful when the environment shifts; all-time maxima assume greater stability. CORAL updates from recent observations under projected constraints, potentially forgetting valuable long-run experience. A small proxy score cannot resolve the trade-off universally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A holiday ad mix can be poor afterward. Recent evidence should matter, while durable safety constraints should not be forgotten.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.02730">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.02730-coral/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b9b80dc33e148828">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:coral" data-paper-title="CORAL: An LLM-Native Harness for Production Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-80652d133f4a6d24">Why not clip each CORAL allocation separately when projecting onto nonnegative values under a total budget?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acoral">CORAL: An LLM-Native Harness for Production Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Per-coordinate clipping fixes negative values but not the coupled sum bound B. Joint projection enforces both. Store the executed configuration with its observations, not the infeasible proposal. The five-round local run verifies constraints and loop executability only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three individually legal allocations of 6 total 18, exceeding a cap of 10. Adjust together and record what actually ran.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.02730">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.02730-coral/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-80652d133f4a6d24">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:effective-training-time" data-paper-title="Optimizing Effective Training Time for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-effective-training-time-8fded34e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2a1f5892e23650ba">Why can effective training time be low despite saturated GPUs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aeffective-training-time">Optimizing Effective Training Time for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ETT counts wall-clock time actually training on new data. Init, compilation, save, publishing, and recovery extend the denominator. Kernel improvements do not fix all pauses. Local lifecycle checks do not estimate production gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Twenty new-data minutes in an hour is about one-third even if GPUs saturate during those minutes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02057">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.02057-effective-training-time/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2a1f5892e23650ba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:effective-training-time" data-paper-title="Optimizing Effective Training Time for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-aef5009086049e42">How does stage accounting choose between optimizing compilation, recovery, and kernels?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aeffective-training-time">Optimizing Effective Training Time for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate new-data training from lifecycle losses, then identify avoidable time and owners. If training occupies little of the run, reducing interruptions can matter more than faster operators.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Cutting one recovery in a run with ten training minutes and 30 recovery minutes can beat a 10% kernel speedup.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02057">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.02057-effective-training-time/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aef5009086049e42">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:effective-training-time" data-paper-title="Optimizing Effective Training Time for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d25e0706c7f774fb">Why can ETT, stable samples/s, and MFU suggest different priorities?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aeffective-training-time">Optimizing Effective Training Time for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Throughput measures training speed; MFU measures compute utilization; ETT measures new-data share over the full lifecycle. More failures or compilation can erase faster kernels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Steps can be 20% faster while frequent restarts reduce daily progress.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02057">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.02057-effective-training-time/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d25e0706c7f774fb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:effective-training-time" data-paper-title="Optimizing Effective Training Time for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7f33374785e1c483">Why define overlap and recovery replay in ETT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aeffective-training-time">Optimizing Effective Training Time for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use actual wall time and count only training on new data. Do not double-count asynchronous save overlap or count replayed old batches as progress. Attribution can overlap without changing ratio accounting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Five overlapping minutes do not make an hour 65 minutes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02057">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.02057-effective-training-time/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7f33374785e1c483">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:evopilot" data-paper-title="Verify, Don&#x27;t Trust: Agentic Model Development for Video Discovery Retrieval at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-evopilot-795a30ed" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9c17b6bb0d1f9105">Why can a negative result pass EvoPilot Verify?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aevopilot">Verify, Don&#x27;t Trust: Agentic Model Development for Video Discovery Retrieval at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Verify checks artifact integrity and comparison protocol, not performance direction. A matched, complete regression is valid evidence, and human Review checks interpretation and acceptance. Do not call verification a gain or discard a real negative result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An isolated interaction head that lowers hit rate is negative evidence; a gain after also changing data is not attributable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.21257-evopilot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9c17b6bb0d1f9105">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:evopilot" data-paper-title="Verify, Don&#x27;t Trust: Agentic Model Development for Video Discovery Retrieval at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e00f149074d02130">Why does EvoPilot treat a matched two-arm comparison, not a successful training job, as evidence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aevopilot">Verify, Don&#x27;t Trust: Agentic Model Development for Video Discovery Retrieval at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One artifact cannot attribute improvement. EvoPilot matches base, data, evaluator, and output depth, allowing only the approved treatment and checking actual artifact state and provenance. Extra changes invalidate comparison; verification can pass for a negative result and is not release approval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new interaction layer trained twice as long cannot claim sole credit until budgets are matched.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.21257-evopilot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e00f149074d02130">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:evopilot" data-paper-title="Verify, Don&#x27;t Trust: Agentic Model Development for Video Discovery Retrieval at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-482826e1007f31c0">Why is reusing a high-quality historical baseline not necessarily a matched treatment comparison?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aevopilot">Verify, Don&#x27;t Trust: Agentic Model Development for Video Discovery Retrieval at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Its base, data, evaluator, or output depth may differ. Match both arms so the approved treatment is the only actual change. More seeds estimate variance but cannot fix a mismatched comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A model with ten output layers versus a five-layer historical baseline did not only change its interaction head.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.21257-evopilot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-482826e1007f31c0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:evopilot" data-paper-title="Verify, Don&#x27;t Trust: Agentic Model Development for Video Discovery Retrieval at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d1d591c91723507">Why read EvoPilot final state and provenance from actual artifacts rather than scheduler success?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aevopilot">Verify, Don&#x27;t Trust: Agentic Model Development for Video Discovery Retrieval at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A job can partially fail, use the wrong config, or leave stale files. Missing final state, version, or actual differences must fail closed. The local check rejects output-depth mismatch, demonstrating validation of execution rather than declarations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A completed job with missing metrics cannot reuse last round&#x27;s JSON as current evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.21257-evopilot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d1d591c91723507">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:evorec" data-paper-title="EvoRec: Self-Evolving Agentic Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-evorec-ed228584" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b33ffe7f74179c8b">Why does EvoRec distill optimization skills as well as evolving models?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aevorec">EvoRec: Self-Evolving Agentic Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Code alone loses what was attempted and where it worked, leading to repeated failures. Skill Evolver summarizes durable experiments to inform future Research and Code Agent proposals. A skill is bounded evidence, not a rule exempt from verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Record that strengthening content helps under a validated short-history condition, not just the final two-tower model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28368">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.28368-evorec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b33ffe7f74179c8b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:evorec" data-paper-title="EvoRec: Self-Evolving Agentic Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d7f3d1db570aa7ca">What does EvoRec&#x27;s Skill Evolver evolve beyond preserving final model code?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aevorec">EvoRec: Self-Evolving Agentic Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Code and weights do not record how a useful change was found or under which conditions. Skill Evolver distills reusable optimization skills from durable experiment memory for future Research and Code Agents. Skills still require actual execution and validation before generalization claims.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sampler helps only the long tail; remember both effective and failed slices, and test on the next dataset rather than copying the champion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28368">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.28368-evorec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d7f3d1db570aa7ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:evorec" data-paper-title="EvoRec: Self-Evolving Agentic Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-47950852691d04f6">How does EvoRec skill memory change exploration compared with fixed grid search?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aevorec">EvoRec: Self-Evolving Agentic Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed grid repeats predefined configurations; remembered skills can reprioritize or combine methods from prior feedback. Competition among a few preset skills validates only bounded control flow, not open-ended invention. Select on validation; test must not guide iteration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A skill library can prioritize a useful representation transform instead of running ten fixed trials; three skills do not prove arbitrary architecture discovery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28368">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.28368-evorec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-47950852691d04f6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:evorec" data-paper-title="EvoRec: Self-Evolving Agentic Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c437ad23d283a87d">Why retain data protocols and failure conditions in EvoRec memory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aevorec">EvoRec: Self-Evolving Agentic Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A winning name cannot establish applicability. Bind the candidate to validation, observations, and constraints, including failures, and execute real operators when reusing skills. A registry label is not integration, and three local generations establish only the tested space.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Record better matched-budget results on sparse histories and that long histories remain unverified, rather than declaring content towers always better.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28368">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.28368-evorec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c437ad23d283a87d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:evoskillrec" data-paper-title="EvoSkillRec: Skill-Genome Evolution for Recommender Architecture Discovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-evoskillrec-7ef949da" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3735285efdd844ab">Why require executable skill I/O contracts in EvoSkillRec?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aevoskillrec">EvoSkillRec: Skill-Genome Evolution for Recommender Architecture Discovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Natural-language names do not ensure composability. Types make genomes executable and uniformly evaluable but are only the first check; semantics and recommendation quality need validation and promotion separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sequence encoder can feed a vector head, but a candidate-set consumer needs an explicit conversion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34552">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.34552-evoskillrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3735285efdd844ab">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:evoskillrec" data-paper-title="EvoSkillRec: Skill-Genome Evolution for Recommender Architecture Discovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-11fbd5c6574e563d">Why type-check adjacent skills in a genome instead of chaining high-scoring modules arbitrarily?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aevoskillrec">EvoSkillRec: Skill-Genome Evolution for Recommender Architecture Discovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Individually good modules may have incompatible shapes and semantics. Check input/output contracts, construct executable candidates, evaluate validation, and store only promoted combinations. Names and types alone do not integrate a skill; three local seeds check composition and state transitions, not capability rankings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An item-vector producer cannot feed a full-history consumer without a suitable adapter and semantic validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34552">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.34552-evoskillrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-11fbd5c6574e563d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:evoskillrec" data-paper-title="EvoSkillRec: Skill-Genome Evolution for Recommender Architecture Discovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b51a0203ac02a2fe">How does validation promotion protect EvoSkillRec&#x27;s reuse library versus keeping every skill?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aevoskillrec">EvoSkillRec: Skill-Genome Evolution for Recommender Architecture Discovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Only innovations exceeding a baseline threshold become reusable, reducing propagation of untested or harmful modules. The threshold is still bounded by budget and data, and neither type checks nor repeated test selection establish quality. Keep failures as failures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Record a shape-correct module that lowered validation, but do not promote it as a default skill.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34552">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.34552-evoskillrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b51a0203ac02a2fe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:evoskillrec" data-paper-title="EvoSkillRec: Skill-Genome Evolution for Recommender Architecture Discovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-aaaed1d71fd23064">Why is matching final tensor width insufficient for skill type checks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aevoskillrec">EvoSkillRec: Skill-Genome Evolution for Recommender Architecture Discovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>B×d user vectors, B×C×d candidate tensors, and B×T×d sequence states have distinct roles. Check batch, candidate, and time semantics, then execute and evaluate. Local state-transition diagnostics do not rank capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Broadcasting one user vector over all candidates can run but loses candidate differences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:forte" data-paper-title="FORTE: A Production Framework for Feature Evaluation and Deprecation in Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-forte-d5b8210d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-40320b35fc4a7114">Why is feature retirement a lifecycle task rather than an importance ranking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aforte">FORTE: A Production Framework for Feature Evaluation and Deprecation in Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Features may feed multiple heads and systems, and training can restore reliance. Audit time stability, joint deletion, retraining, online evidence, and lineage before retiring all consumers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The main click head may not use a field that fraud models still require.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13806">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13806-forte/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-40320b35fc4a7114">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:forte" data-paper-title="FORTE: A Production Framework for Feature Evaluation and Deprecation in Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6ba8284366c5569d">Why require joint perturbation, retraining, and consumer review when each feature seems unnecessary alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aforte">FORTE: A Production Framework for Feature Evaluation and Deprecation in Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Redundant features compensate during one-at-a-time tests. Check weak dependence over time and across heads, then joint removal and retraining, followed by every downstream consumer. One neutral run is not deletion authority.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Age and age buckets can substitute for each other, yet deleting both can hurt new-user tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13806">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13806-forte/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6ba8284366c5569d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:forte" data-paper-title="FORTE: A Production Framework for Feature Evaluation and Deprecation in Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f74a47ab0fc224b5">What do frozen perturbation and retraining answer separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aforte">FORTE: A Production Framework for Feature Evaluation and Deprecation in Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Perturbation measures current reliance; retraining tests adaptation to absence. Neither covers all online effects. Redundancy can hide reliance, and retraining does not erase a failed time gate. Local three-seed baseline retention is a valid negative.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Age removal can hurt a frozen model but recover after retraining; joint removal can hurt despite harmless single deletion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13806">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13806-forte/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f74a47ab0fc224b5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:forte" data-paper-title="FORTE: A Production Framework for Feature Evaluation and Deprecation in Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-de0c178c54f394ff">Why can signed_change be negative, and how does VirtualBatch isolate frozen dependence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aforte">FORTE: A Production Framework for Feature Evaluation and Deprecation in Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Higher-is-better perturbation minus baseline is negative for damage. Reuse dense/sparse/ragged inputs and perturbation maps while switching references; parameter digests rule out updates. Joint effects cannot be summed from individual effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>AUC 0.80→0.79 shows harm, not benefit; training during the probe would change its meaning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13806">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13806-forte/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-de0c178c54f394ff">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:memory-layer" data-paper-title="Memory Layer: Train the In-Model Cache for Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-memory-layer-0d31a0b7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d309a881f527fd6">Why read the same representation in training, evaluation, and serving for Memory Layer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amemory-layer">Memory Layer: Train the In-Model Cache for Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta / Instagram Reels</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Using fresh tower outputs only in training and old external cache online creates mismatch, with misses another distribution. Training writes the internal table; scoring reads it consistently and retains always-on features on misses. Record missingness and age because consistency does not ensure freshness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reading one shared table avoids training on the latest movie vector while serving a different version, but entries can still be stale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25110">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.25110-memory-layer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d309a881f527fd6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:memory-layer" data-paper-title="Memory Layer: Train the In-Model Cache for Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-af7939892d02952f">Why embed the item cache as a sparse model parameter table in Memory Layer instead of publishing it externally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amemory-layer">Memory Layer: Train the In-Model Cache for Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta / Instagram Reels</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fresh tower outputs in training and old cache values at serving differ, and a miss bypass creates a third distribution. Model writeback and reads let training adapt to cache semantics; always-on features score misses. This changes dependencies and train–serve consistency, not guaranteed freshness or zero read cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Training on today&#x27;s item vector but serving yesterday&#x27;s can drift. An internal cache aligns the read path, while creator or topic features still score misses.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25110">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.25110-memory-layer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-af7939892d02952f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:memory-layer" data-paper-title="Memory Layer: Train the In-Model Cache for Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-827dab223ef80fd9">How does internal writeback change consistency and maintenance versus periodic full external cache publication?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amemory-layer">Memory Layer: Train the In-Model Cache for Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta / Instagram Reels</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Coupling writes to training events avoids mismatch from a separate publisher. External rollout gives central control but can lag and miss items. Internal tables still have capacity, concurrency, and versioning concerns; always-on is a miss fallback. The local structure check does not establish Meta throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Training updates item A immediately while unseen items stay old; periodic publishing changes the whole table at once. Hit rate alone cannot rank these schedules.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25110">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.25110-memory-layer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-827dab223ef80fd9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:memory-layer" data-paper-title="Memory Layer: Train the In-Model Cache for Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e90d4036e6663eba">Why is Memory Layer&#x27;s η=1 writeback not ordinary small-step SGD on M[i]?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amemory-layer">Memory Layer: Train the In-Model Cache for Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta / Instagram Reels</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It overwrites the entry with the tower output rather than moving an old value gradually along a gradient. Read from the table, zero the missing component, and retain general attributes. Check write error, coverage, and staleness; calling the table trainable does not override assignment semantics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If the new output is [1, 2, 3], the entry should equal it after writeback, not move one tenth of the way from the old value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25110">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.25110-memory-layer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e90d4036e6663eba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:nova" data-paper-title="NOVA: A Verification-Aware Agent Harness for Architecture Evolution in Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-nova-6f1301b9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-65efab2b17892552">Why isn&#x27;t NOVA&#x27;s architecture gradient an ordinary backpropagation gradient?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Anova">NOVA: A Verification-Aware Agent Harness for Architecture Evolution in Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It summarizes architecture changes, diagnostics, and metrics as an agent control signal. Directional feedback is not a derivative of a differentiable parameter objective; it cannot differentiate code end to end or guarantee improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: &#x27;Widening exceeded budget; changing the gate hurt validation&#x27; guides a proposal without defining derivatives for Python characters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.27243-nova/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-65efab2b17892552">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:nova" data-paper-title="NOVA: A Verification-Aware Agent Harness for Architecture Evolution in Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1fd1d6f99b8afe4f">Why does NOVA separate structural semantics, execution, offline effectiveness, and online impact?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Anova">NOVA: A Verification-Aware Agent Harness for Architecture Evolution in Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Runnable code can still violate intended architecture or harm quality. NOVA uses change history and diagnosis to propose updates, then increasingly expensive checks to reject obvious failures early. Offline success still requires independent online evidence; local execution is diagnostic only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An incorrectly wired task head can pass tensor checks but fail semantics. A structurally correct change can still regress on validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.27243-nova/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1fd1d6f99b8afe4f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:nova" data-paper-title="NOVA: A Verification-Aware Agent Harness for Architecture Evolution in Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3c68b7b618e25f7c">Why can&#x27;t NOVA&#x27;s semantic architecture checks replace ordinary runtime tests or vice versa?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Anova">NOVA: A Verification-Aware Agent Harness for Architecture Evolution in Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shape-compatible code can violate task wiring or defining information flow. Semantic checks test intent, execution checks runnable behavior, and offline/online stages test value. Lower training loss does not justify skipping semantics. The local candidate workflow has no production A/B.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A purchase head wired to click labels can train and lower loss; semantic checks should catch it before deployment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.27243-nova/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3c68b7b618e25f7c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:nova" data-paper-title="NOVA: A Verification-Aware Agent Harness for Architecture Evolution in Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f549c47146369669">What outputs should distinguish actual validation from simulated online impact after NOVA selection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Anova">NOVA: A Verification-Aware Agent Harness for Architecture Evolution in Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Candidates, shape failures, validation scores, and promotion logs can be measured. Without traffic, online stages are simulations or diagnostics, not deployments. Use test only to evaluate the final selection, and record successful skills and prohibited directions in an auditable form.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Rejecting an intentionally bad shape demonstrates an execution gate. Passing simulated impact is not a user experiment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.27243-nova/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f549c47146369669">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:prompt-generation" data-paper-title="Prompt Generation Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-prompt-generation-d1640558" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cc9e170b1b09019e">Why separate feature type from processing components in Prompt Generation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprompt-generation">Prompt Generation Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao Search</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Text, embedding, combo, and sequence say what the input is; preprocessing, projection, and merger say how to transform it. Orthogonal configuration composes without changing model code, but bad configuration can lose data or introduce skew.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A title and a behavior sequence can reuse component families with different settings; text does not imply one fixed pipeline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11326">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.11326-prompt-generation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cc9e170b1b09019e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:prompt-generation" data-paper-title="Prompt Generation Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d412e12f27fcb01">Why configure Prompt Generation&#x27;s preprocessor, projector, and merger with templates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprompt-generation">Prompt Generation Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao Search</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate training and serving implementations drift. One protocol composes cleaning, projection, and fusion/compression with common interpretation. Merger changes token cost and information loss, not merely text assembly. Mean compression does not justify discarding all order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Configure cleaning, projection, and pooling for one title token in both paths; truncating to ten words only on one side creates skew.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
