<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:prompt-generation" data-paper-title="Prompt Generation Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bc543930148110c9">What are the defaults and costs of parameterless mean merger versus learned compression?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprompt-generation">Prompt Generation Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao Search</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Mean pooling is simple, cheap, and consistent without new weights. It loses order and details. Learned compression is flexible but adds cost and overfitting. Compression ratio is not relevance evidence, and mean need not fit every feature.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Pool redundant item attributes, but averaging a history with negation and ordering can lose critical meaning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11326">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.11326-prompt-generation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bc543930148110c9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:prompt-generation" data-paper-title="Prompt Generation Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-64a9ffca7a083428">Why check PG_train(x,c)=PG_serve(x,c) by replaying raw serving features?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprompt-generation">Prompt Generation Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao Search</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Matching JSON does not ensure tokenizer, dependencies, truncation, or missingness match. Replay inputs and compare final tensors with versioned interpreters/configurations. Validation selected Title but test regressed; shorter compression does not establish effectiveness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If serving strips model numbers but training retains them, replay reveals skew despite the same configuration name.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11326">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.11326-prompt-generation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-64a9ffca7a083428">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:radar" data-paper-title="RADAR: Recall Augmentation through Deferred Asynchronous Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-radar-206d8edd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bfe5d1773a5c7047">Why is RADAR&#x27;s cached top-k a nomination rather than guaranteed exposure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aradar">RADAR: Recall Augmentation through Deferred Asynchronous Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It was selected under previous history and still competes with live candidates under current needs and eligibility. A cached score is neither exposure nor a click. Distinguish nominations to assess freshness and downstream value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A cached movie can be filtered because the user watched it or now wants children&#x27;s content.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.07261">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2506.07261-radar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bfe5d1773a5c7047">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:radar" data-paper-title="RADAR: Recall Augmentation through Deferred Asynchronous Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f22b0db4a797c31d">Why use asynchronous post-request ranking to supplement retrieval for the next RADAR request?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aradar">RADAR: Recall Augmentation through Deferred Asynchronous Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A strong ranker cannot usually scan the entire catalog within request latency. RADAR does the expensive scan afterward, caches good candidates, and merges them with live retrieval next time. Old history makes caches stale, so live retrieval still captures new intent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Precompute likely movies after one visit and add them on the next, while live retrieval uses newly observed clicks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.07261">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2506.07261-radar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f22b0db4a797c31d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:radar" data-paper-title="RADAR: Recall Augmentation through Deferred Asynchronous Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f162747603870018">How does RADAR&#x27;s prior-request cache differ from a predicted future pair-latent cache?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aradar">RADAR: Recall Augmentation through Deferred Asynchronous Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>RADAR caches selected item IDs under previous history. Pair-latent caching stores intermediate interactions for specific user–item pairs. Reuse, misses, and invalidation differ, so one hit rate cannot represent both costs or establish a quality ordering.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reusing a movie list saves nomination; intermediate vectors are different artifacts and may still need current scoring.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.07261">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2506.07261-radar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f162747603870018">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:radar" data-paper-title="RADAR: Recall Augmentation through Deferred Asynchronous Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-10c293e7dee1f7e0">Why deduplicate and recheck eligibility when merging RADAR live and cached top-k?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aradar">RADAR: Recall Augmentation through Deferred Asynchronous Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Old items may be unavailable, consumed, or ineligible. Merge by item ID and preserve provenance for incremental evaluation. Record cache generation time and history cutoff; the next target cannot enter the async job ahead of time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Drop a listing that filled since yesterday and count a movie retrieved by both channels only once.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.07261">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2506.07261-radar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-10c293e7dee1f7e0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rec-distill" data-paper-title="Rec-Distill: An Industrial Distillation Pipeline for Large-Scale Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-rec-distill-367afce1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6ffcb019fb96fa25">Why asynchronously share black-box teacher logits across Rec-Distill students?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arec-distill">Rec-Distill: An Industrial Distillation Pipeline for Large-Scale Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin / TikTok</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Running a large teacher for every student call is expensive. Reuse outputs generated during training and let students consume them on separate schedules. Sampling and freshness still need calibration and versioning. Black-box exchange reduces coupling but hides intermediate teacher states.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two small models can consume one batch of teacher scores without running the teacher themselves, provided sample and version provenance are known.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29755">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.29755-rec-distill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6ffcb019fb96fa25">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rec-distill" data-paper-title="Rec-Distill: An Industrial Distillation Pipeline for Large-Scale Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-995da271649e534d">Why correct Rec-Distill teacher sampling probabilities and distill into an auxiliary tower rather than the serving main tower?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arec-distill">Rec-Distill: An Industrial Distillation Pipeline for Large-Scale Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin / TikTok</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different sampling makes logits represent different probabilities. Correct to the student convention, then train aux on labels and distillation while transferring through shared layers. Main only uses true labels and serves, reducing direct calibration distortion. Teacher quality and freshness still matter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A teacher downsampling negatives more aggressively cannot supply raw click probabilities unchanged. Correct it and give soft supervision to aux.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29755">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.29755-rec-distill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-995da271649e534d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rec-distill" data-paper-title="Rec-Distill: An Industrial Distillation Pipeline for Large-Scale Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-480b099c9b0f77c3">What does main/aux distillation protect versus directly fitting serving main to the teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arec-distill">Rec-Distill: An Industrial Distillation Pipeline for Large-Scale Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin / TikTok</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Main keeps the real-label objective, while aux learns both real and teacher labels and transfers indirectly through the shared backbone. This reduces direct calibration bias but is not full isolation. The strong local teacher still transferred negatively.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Aux can learn relative knowledge while main fits clicks; fitting uncorrected probabilities directly can copy the wrong baseline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29755">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.29755-rec-distill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-480b099c9b0f77c3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rec-distill" data-paper-title="Rec-Distill: An Industrial Distillation Pipeline for Large-Scale Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ed85a422881b5223">Why report raw student and teacher metrics when the Rec-Distill transferability denominator is small?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arec-distill">Rec-Distill: An Industrial Distillation Pipeline for Large-Scale Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin / TikTok</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>η is student distillation gain divided by available teacher gain. Near zero, it is unstable. Teacher is not a serving baseline and arms need matching schedules and candidates. Report negative transfer instead of reframing lower head share as success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Tiny student changes can yield large ratios when the teacher barely exceeds the student. Show all three raw metrics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29755">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.29755-rec-distill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ed85a422881b5223">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recevolve" data-paper-title="RecEvolve: A Knowledge-Driven Autonomous Agent System for Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-recevolve-55072983" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5016e08e383200b4">Why aren&#x27;t RecEvolve&#x27;s knowledge base and runnable model artifacts interchangeable?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecevolve">RecEvolve: A Knowledge-Driven Autonomous Agent System for Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The knowledge base stores proposals, protocols, findings, and failures for later choices. Artifacts store parameters and configuration for execution. Promotion evidence must link to the specific runnable version.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: &#x27;The content branch won&#x27; cannot be rerun without config, and bare weights do not show how they beat the champion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01622">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.01622-recevolve/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5016e08e383200b4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recevolve" data-paper-title="RecEvolve: A Knowledge-Driven Autonomous Agent System for Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-372bb80dd4440915">Why put gates, independent validation, and rollback outside the RecEvolve research agent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecevolve">RecEvolve: A Knowledge-Driven Autonomous Agent System for Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Agents can propose useful mutations or exploit a metric. External gates reject invalid candidates, then independent validation compares against the champion. Atomically promote only evidence-backed gains; otherwise retain the incumbent and record failure. Keep test out of the search loop.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reject an illegally sharp low-temperature candidate; keep the champion if another candidate runs but scores worse on validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01622">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.01622-recevolve/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-372bb80dd4440915">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recevolve" data-paper-title="RecEvolve: A Knowledge-Driven Autonomous Agent System for Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c025052f0584af9e">Why can an external critic gate reduce metric gaming compared with agent self-evaluation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecevolve">RecEvolve: A Knowledge-Driven Autonomous Agent System for Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Self-review can favor proposals or shortcuts. An executable external gate fixes allowable changes and independent validation decides promotion. It governs evidence, not innovation, and test cannot feed routine search.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reject an extreme temperature by a fixed constraint rather than accept the agent&#x27;s assurance it did not cheat.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01622">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.01622-recevolve/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c025052f0584af9e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recevolve" data-paper-title="RecEvolve: A Knowledge-Driven Autonomous Agent System for Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8790c407791febbd">Why finish validation artifacts before atomically updating the RecEvolve champion pointer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecevolve">RecEvolve: A Knowledge-Driven Autonomous Agent System for Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Incomplete training, missing metrics, and interrupted writes must not overwrite a working incumbent. Verify terminal state and J before switching the pointer. No promotion is a valid outcome, and small local effects do not establish online gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A half-written checkpoint should leave the champion pointing to the old complete model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01622">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.01622-recevolve/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8790c407791febbd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-51f56bee15d21b4e">Why discretize RecHarness architecture changes into finite arms?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecharness">RecHarness: A Bandit-Routed Agentic Harness for Self-Evolving Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong Agricultural University (Kuaishou internship)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Explicit actions support gain and uncertainty estimates for budget allocation, with feedback guiding future trials. The bandit manages experiments, not direct recommendation. Predefined actions limit the search space.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Widening, gate replacement, and adding content are separate arms, not arbitrary novel code generated from scratch.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recharness" data-paper-title="RecHarness: A Bandit-Routed Agentic Harness for Self-Evolving Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1259497038b725b8">Why does RecHarness allocate experiments by gain and uncertainty rather than always choose the best observed architecture?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecharness">RecHarness: A Bandit-Routed Agentic Harness for Self-Evolving Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong Agricultural University (Kuaishou internship)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Greedy mean selection can abandon underexplored directions too early. Confidence bonuses let uncertain arms receive experiments and winners inform later candidates. It allocates finite research budget, not globally optimal architectures, and gains require one validation protocol.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An arm tried once may merit exploration against a slightly stronger arm tried ten times; final choice still needs independent test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29241">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.29241-recharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1259497038b725b8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recharness" data-paper-title="RecHarness: A Bandit-Routed Agentic Harness for Self-Evolving Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d0deb0712d9b51f7">When is UCB preferable to equal round-robin experiments?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecharness">RecHarness: A Bandit-Routed Agentic Harness for Self-Evolving Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong Agricultural University (Kuaishou internship)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It spends more on high or uncertain gains rather than repeatedly testing poor arms. Nonstationarity and unequal evaluation noise can distort estimates. Exploration does not correct unfair baselines or leakage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An arm with five regressions can receive less budget than a promising arm, provided exploration avoids premature rejection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29241">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.29241-recharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d0deb0712d9b51f7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recharness" data-paper-title="RecHarness: A Bandit-Routed Agentic Harness for Self-Evolving Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-853a202b59350215">How handle RecHarness na=0 and multi-round records without fabricated trials?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecharness">RecHarness: A Bandit-Routed Agentic Harness for Self-Evolving Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong Agricultural University (Kuaishou internship)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Prioritize untested arms or define infinite exploration explicitly. Increment counts only for real completed trials with fixed validation outcomes. Persist actual state on interruption; submission is not feedback. Small proxies do not establish production research throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Record training failure as a failure, not a zero validation reward or successful completed trial.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rocs" data-paper-title="ROCS: Request-Oriented Compute Sharing for Efficient Large-Scale Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-rocs-28113d9d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-90441741441e8286">What are the units of computation in ROCS: one request and its candidates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arocs">ROCS: Request-Oriented Compute Sharing for Efficient Large-Scale Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A request contains user-side context. Candidates are separate items scored within it. They share user input but have separate features and outputs. More candidates do not mean more independent requests. Distinguish these axes to identify reusable versus per-candidate work.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One user opening a page that scores one hundred items is one request with one hundred candidates, not one hundred user requests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27744">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.27744-rocs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-90441741441e8286">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rocs" data-paper-title="ROCS: Request-Oriented Compute Sharing for Efficient Large-Scale Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a037f568e876e729">Why does ROCS need candidate isolation to avoid redoing user computation for every candidate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arocs">ROCS: Request-Oriented Compute Sharing for Efficient Large-Scale Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A state that has read one candidate is not a common cache. Generalized Layer Masking preserves isolation and Deep Cross Attention delays candidate interaction, so a request representation is computed once. Kernel broadcasting further reduces copies. The local in-process microbenchmark compares repeated and shared encoding, not full production throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One request scores a hundred items. Encode the user independently, then broadcast to each item branch. If item A contaminates user state first, reusing it for item B leaks information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27744">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.27744-rocs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a037f568e876e729">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rocs" data-paper-title="ROCS: Request-Oriented Compute Sharing for Efficient Large-Scale Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a7629b435887d373">Are request-representation sharing and IKBO&#x27;s reduced on-device copying the same optimization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arocs">ROCS: Request-Oriented Compute Sharing for Efficient Large-Scale Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Model information flow makes representations shareable; device broadcasting moves a valid shared representation into candidate computation efficiently. Caching a user vector can verify the division of work, not a production broadcast kernel or throughput. Each layer needs its own implementation and measurements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>First ensure candidate inputs cannot contaminate the user state. In-process cache timings do not replace GPU broadcast kernel measurements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27744">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.27744-rocs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a7629b435887d373">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rocs" data-paper-title="ROCS: Request-Oriented Compute Sharing for Efficient Large-Scale Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c3d495c5df8a7b41">Does local ROCS implement production GLM masks and IKBO CUDA broadcasting?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arocs">ROCS: Request-Oriented Compute Sharing for Efficient Large-Scale Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It covers the division between shared representation and scoring, not a specialized kernel or Meta cluster. Architectural reuse and on-device broadcasting need distinct evidence, and throughput claims require measurement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A Python loop reusing one vector does not show that a GPU kernel shares loads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27744">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.27744-rocs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c3d495c5df8a7b41">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:self-evolving-rec" data-paper-title="Self-Evolving Recommendation System: End-To-End Autonomous Model Optimization With LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4b4c2af3f199e061">Does Self-Evolving Rec&#x27;s journal store model parameters or experimental knowledge?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aself-evolving-rec">Self-Evolving Recommendation System: End-To-End Autonomous Model Optimization With LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It records proposals, execution, and protocol-bound outcomes. This is distinct from checkpoint storage. A prose plan without runnable candidates and evaluation is not an experiment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Record a failed optimizer comparison so the next iteration avoids repeating it.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:self-evolving-rec" data-paper-title="Self-Evolving Recommendation System: End-To-End Autonomous Model Optimization With LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a0ff42610abe6dfe">Why should the outer state machine control real A/B promotion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aself-evolving-rec">Self-Evolving Recommendation System: End-To-End Autonomous Model Optimization With LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Offline agents cheaply screen ideas but cannot capture all user and serving constraints. The outer loop controls safety, resources, promotion, and journal feedback. Local loops do not replace live production A/B.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reject an offline winner with excess latency; record a later approved experiment so future rounds learn.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10226">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.10226-self-evolving-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a0ff42610abe6dfe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:self-evolving-rec" data-paper-title="Self-Evolving Recommendation System: End-To-End Autonomous Model Optimization With LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-937788d1136b4b7b">How does bilevel optimization differ from a hyperparameter sweep?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aself-evolving-rec">Self-Evolving Recommendation System: End-To-End Autonomous Model Optimization With LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Inner training explores architecture, optimizer, or reward; outer governance manages online goals, resources, safety, and accumulated knowledge. Tuning can support the inner layer but does not replace the outer loop.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A learning-rate sweep does not decide whether to spend live traffic or archive failures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10226">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.10226-self-evolving-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-937788d1136b4b7b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aself-evolving-rec">Self-Evolving Recommendation System: End-To-End Autonomous Model Optimization With LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:solaris" data-paper-title="SOLARIS: Speculative Offloading of Latent-bAsed Representation for Inference Scaling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-91c05cfa4ac73637">Why predict future user–item pairs before computing SOLARIS latents?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asolaris">SOLARIS: Speculative Offloading of Latent-bAsed Representation for Inference Scaling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Computing all pairs online is expensive. Predict likely pairs and asynchronously precompute them for lightweight consumption. Misses need fallback and wrong guesses waste budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Prepare representations for a shortlist instead of an entire catalog.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.12110">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.12110-solaris/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-91c05cfa4ac73637">Question link</a></p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:solaris" data-paper-title="SOLARIS: Speculative Offloading of Latent-bAsed Representation for Inference Scaling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2fe75d5f35fcadd4">Why cache predicted pair latents instead of one user vector?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asolaris">SOLARIS: Speculative Offloading of Latent-bAsed Representation for Inference Scaling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Deep interactions depend on a particular item. Predict likely pairs, compute asynchronously, use hits and fallback on misses. Coverage, freshness, and budget matter. Future outcomes can supervise training, not online selection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Precompute ten likely products, but serve an unexpected one through fallback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:solaris" data-paper-title="SOLARIS: Speculative Offloading of Latent-bAsed Representation for Inference Scaling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6b7fcf1178ba1fc0">How does a latent cache differ from a final list cache?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asolaris">SOLARIS: Speculative Offloading of Latent-bAsed Representation for Inference Scaling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A latent is a middle feature the lightweight ranker can combine with current inputs. A cached list fixes ordering. Latents still age and need version consistency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reusing a latent with today&#x27;s price can change yesterday&#x27;s order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.12110">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.12110-solaris/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6b7fcf1178ba1fc0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<h2 id="qa-29504be389624dcd">What should a SOLARIS cache key capture?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asolaris">SOLARIS: Speculative Offloading of Latent-bAsed Representation for Inference Scaling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>User/item identity, model and feature versions, and validity; define hit and fallback paths. An abstract implementation or hit rate does not prove service latency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not silently reuse a latent from a previous model version.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ug-sep" data-paper-title="Compute Only Once: UG-Separation for Efficient Large Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-ug-sep-25948e1e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f7cb92de7c9f342c">Do UG-Sep user and candidate tokens describe two users?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aug-sep">Compute Only Once: UG-Separation for Efficient Large Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance AML</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. One request has a shared user block and an item-specific candidate block. Isolation controls information flow, not user groups.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Several candidate blocks can reuse the same user&#x27;s history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10455">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.10455-ug-sep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f7cb92de7c9f342c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ug-sep" data-paper-title="Compute Only Once: UG-Separation for Efficient Large Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8145189206c730cf">Why block candidate-to-user flow and then compensate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aug-sep">Compute Only Once: UG-Separation for Efficient Large Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance AML</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Isolation makes user encoding reusable; it may weaken bidirectional expressiveness, so compensation restores interactions in the item scoring path only. Do not cache compensated state as public.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compute one item-free user state for 100 candidates, then apply separate per-item compensation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10455">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.10455-ug-sep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8145189206c730cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ug-sep" data-paper-title="Compute Only Once: UG-Separation for Efficient Large Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ada9a9a1316edf1c">Can Information Compensation turn candidate-conditioned state into reusable cache?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aug-sep">Compute Only Once: UG-Separation for Efficient Large Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance AML</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It restores candidate-specific scoring interactions. Shared state must remain candidate-independent, so caching compensation for another item reintroduces contamination.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Item A&#x27;s compensated state is not general user state for B.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10455">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.10455-ug-sep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ada9a9a1316edf1c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ug-sep" data-paper-title="Compute Only Once: UG-Separation for Efficient Large Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-da3bf12463f029c9">How test whether the UG-Sep mask permits safe sharing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aug-sep">Compute Only Once: UG-Separation for Efficient Large Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance AML</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fix user and vary candidates: protected user representations must stay unchanged while item output may change. Check attention and TokenMixer, not only masks. No production kernels/QPS.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A masked attention path is insufficient if the mixer leaks candidate information back.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10455">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.10455-ug-sep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-da3bf12463f029c9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<details class="ar-learning-guide" markdown="1"><summary>Topic guide and reading order</summary>

## Start with this question

When is a better offline method usable under real requests and continued iteration?

## Takeaway

Move compute to where it is affordable: distillation teaches a light student, request-state sharing avoids repeated encoding, and asynchronous caching removes work from the request path. Automated research tracks hypotheses, execution, validation, and conclusions. Proposing a candidate and actually running and evaluating it are separate. Both research and serving need verifiable execution and independent evaluation.

## Example

An illustrative user encode costs 2 ms and a candidate interaction 0.02 ms. Re-encoding for 100 candidates costs about 202 ms; encoding once and scoring them costs about 4 ms. Real results depend on parallelism, cache, bandwidth, and operator overhead. This is not a production speedup.

## Common pitfall

Compare a distilled student with a same-schedule student, not with the stronger teacher. In-process timing is not GPU-cluster throughput. Search selects on validation only, and cost-closed references must not become executable candidates.

## Reading order

Read Rec-Distill for training-to-serving transfer, ROCS for request reuse, and Self-Evolving RecSys for candidate execution, validation selection, and log feedback. Local mechanisms run, while production serving and A/B remain separate limits.

1. [Rec-Distill: An Industrial Distillation Pipeline for Large-Scale Recommendation Models](../../../../reproductions/2605.29755-rec-distill/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29755)
2. [ROCS: Request-Oriented Compute Sharing for Efficient Large-Scale Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2607.27744-rocs/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27744)
3. [Self-Evolving Recommendation System: End-To-End Autonomous Model Optimization With LLM Agents](../../../../reproductions/2602.10226-self-evolving-rec/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10226)

## Check your understanding

Does writing a new registry name close the research loop if the controller cannot execute or evaluate it?

??? note "Show suggested answer"

    No. Build the candidate, execute its path, obtain comparable validation results, and record failures and limits. A name or proposal is not evidence of improvement.

</details>
